This builds on the original program and adds a full Portland-specific site/regulatory section. Key numbers, at a glance:

**Height limit:** Portland's single-dwelling zones (R5, R7, R10, etc.) are governed by Title 33, Chapter 33.110. R5 — the most common zone for detached houses on standard inner-Portland lots (5,000 sf minimum) — generally restricts residential structures to 30-35 feet, with exact figures and measurement rules varying by zone and site slope.

**Setbacks / property-line proximity:** In R5 zones, front setbacks are 10 feet, side 5 feet, rear 5 feet. That side setback is the number that matters most for "how close can a second story get to neighbors" — it applies to all floors, not just the ground floor.

**Fire-resistant walls near property lines:** Under the Oregon Residential Specialty Code, walls less than 3 feet from a property line must be fire-resistance rated, and projections less than 2 feet are not allowed. Since standard R5 side setback (5 ft) clears that threshold, this mostly becomes a design issue on narrow lots, additions, or any wall that sits closer than 5 ft.

I flagged R5 as a **working assumption, not a confirmed fact** — Portland zoning is parcel-specific, so the brief's Section 11 lists confirming the actual zone (via PortlandMaps.com or BDS) as the top open item before anything gets locked in.

The rest of the brief carries the roof pitch/climate guidance, the load-alignment logic, and the stair placement strategy into the same room-by-room program from before, so it reads as one coherent scope document.
